result:
Lint is clean too. The implementation is complete:

**Summary of changes:**
- `src/types/organization.ts` — added `OwnershipHandoverStatus` and `OwnershipHandover`.
- `src/types/event.ts` — added `organization.ownership_transferred` to `TaskflowEventMap`.
- `src/types/activity.ts` / `src/components/domain/activity/activity-labels.ts` — new `ActivityAction` + label.
- `src/types/notification.ts` / `src/schemas/notification.ts` / `src/server/db/schema/notifications.ts` / notification preferences form — new `ownership_handover` notification kind.
- `src/types/permission.ts` / `src/lib/permissions.ts` — new `org:manage_ownership` action (owner-gated), used only to shape the `PermissionDeniedError` thrown when a non-recorded-owner acts.
- `src/lib/errors.ts` — `OwnershipHandoverError`/`OwnershipHandoverRefusal`, wired into `isDomainError`/`toAppError` as `conflict`.
- `src/server/db/schema/organizations.ts` + `migrate.ts` — new `ownership_handovers` table (and index), included in the fresh-migration path.
- `src/server/repositories/_mappers.ts`, new `ownership-handover-repository.ts`, and `setOwner` in `organization-repository.ts`.
- `src/server/services/organization-service.ts` — the five exported functions (`initiateOwnershipHandover`, `acceptOwnershipHandover`, `declineOwnershipHandover`, `cancelOwnershipHandover`, `getPendingOwnershipHandover`), with lazy 7-day expiry, recorded-owner-only guard, all refusal cases, owner-before-admin role sequencing on acceptance, the `member.role_changed`/`organization.ownership_transferred` events, and the offer notification.
- `src/server/services/member-service.ts` — auto-withdraws any open offer when either party is removed.
- `src/server/services/activity-service.ts` — audits `organization.ownership_transferred`.

Verified with `tsc --noEmit`, the full existing suite (617 tests, all passing), `eslint`, and a scratch end-to-end test exercising the full happy path, every guard/refusal, event payloads, role transitions, auto-withdraw on removal, and lazy expiry (removed afterward, not part of the deliverable).
